description:
What Does a Black Hole Sound Like?

Space is mostly silent, but in the Perseus galaxy cluster a black hole sends pressure waves through hot gas. NASA turned them into sound.

Follow for daily trips through the universe. 🚀

Images: NASA, ESA, ESO and Wikimedia Commons (free licenses, credited in the video file's notes)
Narration: AI voice

#blackhole #space #nasa #astronomy #shorts #science

segments.text: You've heard that space is silent. But a black hole is humming, right now.
It sits in a giant cluster of galaxies called Perseus, about two hundred and forty million light-years away.
segments.headline: The Perseus cluster

segments.text: The cluster is filled with hot gas. And gas can carry sound waves.
segments.headline: Gas carries sound

segments.text: The black hole sends out ripples. Scientists measured the note: a B-flat, fifty-seven octaves below middle C.
That's far too deep for any human ear, more than a quadrillion times too low.
So NASA sped it up until we could hear it. And it sounds like a haunted, rumbling moan.
segments.headline: NASA made it audible
